repositories.name: platform-contracts
repositories.reason: Source of truth for every changed schema: column tags on ingestion.schema.discovered.v1, classification on metadata.dataset.changed.v1 and the metadata-service Column schema, a new steward classification endpoint, masked_columns on the entitlements Decision and query response, and a classification selector on transformation rule bindings (minor release 2.3.0 -> 2.4.0).

repositories.name: platform-sdk
repositories.reason: Typed SDK models drop undeclared fields (ADR-004), so MetadataClient's column model needs classification fields, EntitlementsClient's Decision needs masked_columns, a steward set-classification method is needed, and publish validation must pin contracts 2.4.0.

repositories.name: ingestion-service
repositories.reason: Postgres connectors already read column comments with tags such as 'tags: pii,email' but do not propagate them; they must parse them and emit an optional columns[].tags on ingestion.schema.discovered.v1 (AC1).

repositories.name: metadata-service
repositories.reason: Owns the column model: must derive a suggested classification from ingested tags, store the effective classification per column with steward-override precedence, expose it on GET columns plus a new steward PUT endpoint, and include it in metadata.dataset.changed.v1 (AC1, AC2).

repositories.name: search-indexer
repositories.reason: Strict consumer of metadata.dataset.changed.v1 with a vendored contracts 2.1.0 schema (additionalProperties: false); it would dead-letter every event carrying classification, so it must vendor 2.4.0 and deploy before metadata-service emits the new fields.

repositories.name: entitlements-service
repositories.reason: Only place access decisions are computed (ADR-007): must load column classifications from metadata-service, check the requester's pii:read grant, and return masked_columns in POST /v1/access/decide (AC3).

repositories.name: consumption-gateway
repositories.reason: Single enforcement point for data returned to consumers (ADR-007): must read masked_columns from the decision and mask those columns in POST /v1/query results (AC4).

repositories.name: transformation-service
repositories.reason: Picks rules per column from bindings by data type only; must read column classification via MetadataClient.get_columns and bind PII-format validation rules to PII columns (AC5).

repositories.name: platform-e2e
repositories.reason: Cross-service behaviour is new (tag -> classification -> masked decision -> masked query result, and PII transformation rules), so a new end-to-end suite must be added and run in int per the change playbook.

repositories.name: lineage-service
repositories.reason: Tolerant consumer of metadata.dataset.changed.v1 (reads urn and name only); re-run its contract tests against the 2.4.0 payload to confirm the new column fields are ignored.

repositories.name: notification-service
repositories.reason: Consumes transformation.result.published.v1 (whose results will now include PII rule outcomes and may lower scores) and metadata-service-api via the SDK; re-verify its contract tests and alert thresholds, no code change expected.

considered_not_impacted.name: usage-metering
considered_not_impacted.reason: Consumes only consumption.access.logged.v1, which this plan leaves unchanged (adding masking info to it is an open question).

considered_not_impacted.name: reporting-service
considered_not_impacted.reason: Decommissioned and archived in 2025; the metadata-service README still lists it as a consumer of metadata.dataset.changed.v1, but that listing is out of date.

considered_not_impacted.name: platform-catalog
considered_not_impacted.reason: No new repository-to-repository integration edges are introduced (all calls and topics used already exist in the catalog), so no code or test change; re-check entities when the PRs are reviewed.

considered_not_impacted.name: architecture-docs
considered_not_impacted.reason: Documentation only, with no runtime code or tests; the access-decision, transformation, ingest-to-metadata flows and the consumer registry should be refreshed as a doc follow-up.

contracts.name: ingestion.schema.discovered.v1
contracts.description: Add optional columns[].tags (array of lower-case strings parsed from the source column comment, e.g. ["pii","email"]); stays on .v1 per ADR-009; the only consumer (metadata-service) is tolerant.

contracts.name: metadata.dataset.changed.v1
contracts.description: Add optional dataset.columns[].classification (enum PUBLIC|INTERNAL|CONFIDENTIAL|PII, nullable), classification_source (SOURCE_TAGS|STEWARD, nullable) and tags; change_type enum unchanged (steward overrides publish COLUMNS_CHANGED). Additive per ADR-009 but rejected by the strict search-indexer until it vendors 2.4.0, so search-indexer must ship first.

contracts.name: GET /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns
contracts.description: Column schema gains optional classification, classification_source and tags (same semantics as the event); metadata-service-api 1.4.0 -> 1.5.0.

contracts.name: PUT /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns/{column_name}/classification
contracts.description: New steward endpoint: body {classification: PUBLIC|INTERNAL|CONFIDENTIAL|PII|null, reason?: string}; a value sets a STEWARD override that later ingestion never overwrites, null clears it back to the tag-derived suggestion; returns the updated Column, 404 for unknown dataset/column, 400 for invalid enum; publishes metadata.dataset.changed.v1 (COLUMNS_CHANGED).

contracts.name: POST /v1/access/decide
contracts.description: Decision gains optional masked_columns (array of column names, default []), listing columns classified PII when the principal holds no pii:read grant for the dataset; request body unchanged; entitlements-api 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0.

contracts.name: POST /v1/query
contracts.description: Response rows keep the same keys, but values of masked columns are replaced (strings -> fixed token, other types -> null), and the response gains optional masked_columns listing them; gated by a feature flag; query-api 2.0.0 -> 2.1.0.

contracts.name: POST /v1/rules
contracts.description: Rule bindings gain an optional classification selector (and optional tag selector, e.g. email) next to the data-type selector, so PII-format rules bind to PII columns; GET /v1/rules returns the new optional fields; existing bindings are unchanged.

open_questions: Tag-to-classification mapping: assumed pii -> PII, confidential -> CONFIDENTIAL, internal -> INTERNAL, public -> PUBLIC, highest sensitivity wins, no recognised tag -> null (unclassified). Does data governance own a different or configurable mapping?

Unclassified columns (all existing data before re-ingestion or steward review) are assumed to be not masked, which keeps today's behaviour. Should they instead default to INTERNAL, and is a backfill (forced re-discovery) required before masking is switched on?
Scope of the pii:read grant: global, per domain or per dataset? Who issues it, and is it new grant data in entitlements-service or does it already exist?
Should only PII be masked, or should CONFIDENTIAL also be masked for some principals? The ticket only defines PII masking.

Who is a steward, and how is PUT .../classification authorised? Today metadata-service's PUT owner has no visible auth. Options: an ingress/gateway role, or a classification:write grant checked against entitlements-service, which would add a new metadata-service -> entitlements-service dependency.

Masked value format: the assumption is a fixed string token for string columns and null for other types, plus masked_columns in the response. Do consumers with non-nullable typed schemas need a different format, such as format-preserving masking or hashing?

Derived expressions: consumption-gateway masks by output column name, so SELECT email AS e or upper(email) can bypass masking. Is SQL column-lineage resolution available, and should unresolvable queries over masked columns be rejected (403) or have every derived column masked?

Fail mode: if entitlements-service cannot load column classifications, should the decision deny (fail closed) or allow and mask all columns? Assumed: fail closed, the same as today when dataset metadata is unavailable.

Which PII-format rules exist (email, phone, national-id...), and should they be chosen by source tag? transformation-service needs the tag subtype (e.g. email), which is why tags are exposed on columns.
Should consumption.access.logged.v1 record masked_columns for audit? That would be an additive change read by usage-metering (tolerant), and it is left out of scope here.
Should search-indexer index classification (e.g. allow searching for PII columns), or only accept it in its schema? This plan only requires accepting it.
Version numbers (contracts 2.4.0, platform-sdk 3.5.0, metadata-service-api 1.5.0, entitlements-api 1.3.0, query-api 2.1.0) are inferred from the current versions and semver rules, not confirmed.
